info.name: Booking System API
info.description: Phase 1-6 endpoints for the appointment booking system. Requests are chained with collection variables via test scripts, so running them top to bottom in a folder auto-fills the next request's IDs. Run '0. Auth' first (staff/admin AND customer login) before anything else, then 'List Services' before the booking flow, and 'List Available Slots' before creating a booking. Booking creation is now customer-auth-gated (Phase 6) — every booking-creation request needs {{customerToken}}, set by '0. Auth'. The 'date' variable is recomputed automatically before every request (see the collection's Pre-request Script) so this collection keeps working no matter what day it's actually run on — see that script's comment for why.

exec: // Keeps the shared 'date' variable perpetually valid instead of a one-time hardcoded
// string. Without this, once real-world 'today' passes the date this collection was
// authored on, GET /api/slots would return zero slots for {{date}} for a totally
// unrelated reason to what most of these requests are actually testing: the new
// elapsed-slot filter in backend/src/services/availability.ts excludes any slot whose
// startTime has already passed, and a stale hardcoded date is 100% in the past by
// definition. Always picks a day strictly after today (never 'today' itself), so it
// can't flake based on what time of day the collection happens to run at either -- a
// same-day date could still legitimately have zero slots left if run late in the
// evening, which isn't the scenario these requests are meant to test. Skips Fridays
// to match the seeded resource's closedWeekdays: [5], so the day it lands on is

variable.description: Overwritten automatically before every request by the collection's Pre-request Script — this initial value is just a placeholder, never actually used.

OTP delivery is console-log-only in this project (see customer-accounts-plan.md) — after 'Register Customer' or 'Forgot Password (Customer)' runs, check the backend terminal for a line like '[OTP] EMAIL_VERIFY code for ...: 123456', paste that 6-digit code in here, then run the matching Verify/Reset request.

request.description: Credentials come from the seed script (prisma/seed.ts) — run 'npm run seed' on the backend first. Auto-saves the JWT as adminToken for every request below that needs ADMIN access. Note this is the STAFF login endpoint (/api/auth/login), separate from customer login below — the frontend serves this at /staff/login.
Auto-saves the JWT as staffToken — used to prove STAFF-level endpoints work, and that ADMIN-only endpoints correctly reject a STAFF token.
Same error as a nonexistent email would give — proves the API doesn't leak which emails have accounts.
Lets the frontend verify a stored token is still valid and fetch the current user's role.
Only an ADMIN token can create accounts. Uses {{$timestamp}} in the email so re-running this doesn't collide with a previous run's account. Auto-saves the created email as newStaffEmail.
Same endpoint, but with a STAFF token instead of ADMIN. requireRole(ADMIN) should reject this with 403 — a valid, logged-in user, just not an authorized one for this action.
Should include the seeded admin/staff accounts plus the one just created above.

exec: pm.test('Includes the newly created staff account', () => pm.expect(users.some(u => u.email === pm.collectionVariables.get('newStaffEmail'))).to.be.true);

request.description: Public. Creates an UNVERIFIED customer account and sends a 6-digit OTP — since email delivery is console-log-only in this project (see customer-accounts-plan.md), check the backend terminal, copy the code, and set the 'otpCode' collection variable before running 'Verify Customer Email' below. If you've already registered this email in a previous run, this returns 409 — either change 'customerEmail' or skip to 'Login as Customer'.

Set the 'otpCode' collection variable from the backend console log first (see 'Register Customer'). On success, marks the account verified AND logs the customer in — auto-saves customerToken so you can skip straight to 'Get Customer Profile' below. If the account is already verified this returns 409 — that's fine, just run 'Login as Customer' instead.

Public, separate from staff login (/api/auth/login) — a customer token has kind: 'customer' and can never satisfy a staff-only route, even by accident. Requires the account to already be verified (run 'Register Customer' + 'Verify Customer Email' first if you haven't). Auto-saves customerToken/customerId, overwriting whatever 'Verify Customer Email' set.

item.name: Login as Customer with Wrong Password (expect 401)

request.description: Same generic message a nonexistent email would give — mirrors the staff login's anti-enumeration behavior.
Confirms customerToken is valid and returns the profile shape the frontend uses (no passwordHash).
Public — no token needed. Auto-saves the first service's id/resourceId as collection variables for the requests below.

exec: pm.test('Has at least one seeded service', () => pm.expect(services.length).to.be.above(0));

request.description: As of Phase 5, this endpoint requires login. No Authorization header here on purpose — proves requireAuth actually rejects unauthenticated requests.
Requires STAFF or ADMIN login — using staffToken here to prove STAFF-level read access works. Auto-saves the first resource's businessId — needed for the Holidays & Hours folder below.

ADMIN only. Creates a new resource under the admin's own business — businessId comes from the token, never the body. Omitted working hours fall back to the schema's own defaults (09:00-17:00, no closed days). Auto-saves the created id as newResourceId.
Same endpoint, STAFF token instead of ADMIN — creating a resource is ADMIN-only, same as services and holidays.
ADMIN only. Attaches a new service to one of the admin's own resources — resourceId must belong to the admin's business, or this returns 403. Auto-saves the created service's id as newServiceId.
Same endpoint, STAFF token instead of ADMIN — managing the service catalog is ADMIN-only, same as holidays and resource hours.
ADMIN only. Only fields included in the body are changed — this updates just the price of the service created above.

ADMIN only. Cleans up the service created by 'Add Service (Admin)' — succeeds because it has no bookings against it. Deleting a service that already has bookings would instead return 409 (see services.ts's P2003 handling).

Public — no token needed (browsing slots doesn't require login, only booking one does). Uses resourceId/serviceId from 'List Services'. The 'date' collection variable is auto-computed (always a future day) by the collection's Pre-request Script — see its comment. Response is {slots, note}. Auto-saves the first open slot's startTime.

exec: pm.test('No returned slot has already elapsed', () => {

request.description: No Authorization header on purpose — as of Phase 6, booking a service requires a verified customer account. Proves requireCustomerAuth rejects anonymous requests instead of silently creating an anonymous booking like it used to pre-Phase-6.

Requires a customer token — run '0. Auth' (Register/Verify or Login as Customer) first. Notice there's no customerName/Phone/Email in the body anymore: those are pulled server-side from the logged-in customer's own profile, so a customer can't book 'as' someone else. Books the slot found by 'List Available Slots'. Auto-saves the returned bookingRef.

exec: pm.test('Booking is linked to the customer account', () => pm.expect(booking.customerId).to.eql(pm.collectionVariables.get('customerId')));

request.description: Public lookup by the customer-facing booking reference — no login needed, possession of the reference is the 'auth' here.

Run this right after 'Create Booking (as Customer)' WITHOUT re-running 'List Available Slots' — it reuses the same startTime that's already booked, with a different (fresh) idempotencyKey. Should fail with 409, proving the @@unique([resourceId, startTime]) constraint works.
Run 'List Available Slots' again first to get a fresh, unbooked startTime, THEN run this request. Uses the fixed 'retryKey' collection variable instead of a random guid.
Identical body to 'Idempotent Retry - First Call', including the same idempotencyKey. Should return 200 with the SAME bookingRef instead of creating a duplicate or erroring.

item.name: Slots on a Weekly-Closed Day (expect empty + note)

request.description: Public. The seeded resource has closedWeekdays: [5] (Friday), and closedWeekdayDate defaults to a Friday. Should return an empty slots array plus a note explaining the weekly closure.

item.name: Slots on the Seeded Holiday (expect empty + note)

request.description: Public. holidayDate defaults to the seed script's 'Staff Training Day' holiday. Should return an empty slots array plus a note with the holiday reason.

exec: pm.test('Note mentions the holiday reason', () => pm.expect(body.note).to.include('Staff Training Day'));

request.description: Requires STAFF or ADMIN login. Scoped automatically to the logged-in user's own business — no businessId param needed anymore. Should include the seeded 'Staff Training Day' holiday.
ADMIN only. Creates a new one-off closure for the admin's own business (businessId comes from the token, not the body). Auto-saves the returned holiday's id so 'Delete Holiday' below can clean it up.
Same endpoint as 'Add Holiday', but with a STAFF token — proves managing holidays is ADMIN-only, unlike just viewing them.
Same date as 'Add Holiday' above. The @@unique([businessId, date]) constraint should reject this with 409.
ADMIN only. Cleans up the holiday created by 'Add Holiday'.
ADMIN only. Updates the resource's daily hours and adds Saturday (6) to the weekly closures alongside the seeded Friday (5). Re-run 'List Available Slots' afterward to see the new hours reflected.
Public. Re-fetches slots (in case earlier folders booked some) and saves the first open one as checkinStartTime.

exec: pm.test('Has at least one open slot', () => pm.expect(body.slots.length).to.be.above(0));

request.description: Requires a customer token (run '0. Auth' first). Auto-saves the bookingRef as checkinBookingRef. Response includes a qrCode field (base64 PNG data URL) — paste it into a browser address bar to see the actual QR image.

exec: pm.test('Response includes a qrCode data URL', () => pm.expect(booking.qrCode).to.include('data:image/png;base64'));

request.description: Requires STAFF or ADMIN login — simulates staff scanning the customer's QR. Should succeed since the booking is currently BOOKED.
Same booking, already CHECKED_IN. The state machine should reject this transition.
CHECKED_IN -> COMPLETED, a valid transition.
COMPLETED has no allowed outgoing transitions — proves the state machine rejects this.
Public. Grabs another open slot (different from the one just booked/completed above) for the no-show scenario.
Requires a customer token. Auto-saves bookingRef as noShowBookingRef.
BOOKED -> NO_SHOW, a valid transition (staff manually marking a customer who never arrived).
NO_SHOW has no allowed outgoing transitions — proves a customer can't check in after being marked a no-show.
Requires STAFF or ADMIN login. Should show both test bookings above: one COMPLETED, one NO_SHOW, plus anything else booked for resourceId on this date.

exec: pm.test('Queue includes the completed booking', () => pm.expect(queue.some(b => b.bookingRef === pm.collectionVariables.get('checkinBookingRef'))).to.be.true);
pm.test('Queue includes the no-show booking', () => pm.expect(queue.some(b => b.bookingRef === pm.collectionVariables.get('noShowBookingRef'))).to.be.true);

request.description: Requires STAFF or ADMIN login. Aggregates every resource in the caller's business for one day — booking counts by status, expected vs completed revenue, and up to 5 upcoming bookings. Defaults to today if the date param is omitted.
No Authorization header on purpose — proves this business-data endpoint isn't accidentally public.

Public, always returns the same generic message whether or not the email exists or is already verified — prevents this endpoint from being used to enumerate accounts. If it actually sends a fresh code (unverified account, cooldown expired), check the backend console.
Only name and phone are editable — email is the fixed identifier the account is looked up by everywhere (login, OTP), so it's intentionally not part of this endpoint.

Requires being logged in AND re-proving the current password. Uses the same value for old and new here just so re-running this collection doesn't drift the password out from under 'customerPassword' — change 'newPassword' to something different to actually test it, then update the collection variable to match.
Proves a valid session token alone isn't enough to change the password — re-proving the current one is required, same principle as most account-security flows.
Public, same generic message whether or not the email exists. Sends a PASSWORD_RESET OTP — check the backend console, copy the code into 'otpCode', then run 'Reset Password' below.

Set 'otpCode' from the backend console log first (see 'Forgot Password (Customer)'). Proves identity via the OTP instead of the (forgotten) password. Resets to the same 'customerPassword' value here so the rest of the collection keeps working unmodified.

The logged-in customer's own booking history, most recent first — scoped by the customerId embedded in the token, never a query param. Should include the bookings created in '2. Booking Flow' and '5. Check-in & Queue' above.

Requires STAFF or ADMIN login. Matches by name/email/phone (case-insensitive substring). Lets staff find the Postman test customer registered in '0. Auth' before booking on their behalf, instead of always typing a fresh walk-in. Auto-saves the first match's id as staffCustomerId.

A customer token has kind: 'customer', not 'staff' — requireAuth should reject it outright, proving a customer can never browse the customer directory even though the payload shapes are superficially similar.
Public. Grabs an open slot for the no-account walk-in booking below.

STAFF/ADMIN only. Unlike POST /api/bookings, this trusts staff-typed contact info, since staff are vouching for the person in front of them. customerId is omitted, so the created booking's customerId stays null — same nullable field that covered pre-accounts legacy bookings, now doing double duty for walk-ins too.

item.name: Fresh Slots for Existing-Customer Staff Booking

request.description: Public. Grabs another open slot for the staff-booking-an-existing-customer scenario below.

STAFF/ADMIN only. Uses staffCustomerId from 'Search Customers (Staff)' — name/phone/email are looked up server-side from that customer's profile, not retyped, so this can't accidentally attach the booking to the wrong contact details. This booking should then show up in that customer's 'List My Bookings' (folder 7).
A customer token can't hit staff-only endpoints, even one that superficially looks like a booking-creation endpoint — kind: 'customer' fails requireAuth before requireRole is ever checked.
